name: Troppau
classification_notes: Geometric sans proportions fused with sharp blackletter insets, referencing the German-influenced history of the Czech city Opava (Troppau), place this in the display category as a genre-blending face.
summary: A geometric sans fused with sharp blackletter insets, named after a Czech city shaped by German influence.
description: Troppau takes a geometric sans skeleton and cuts sharp blackletter details into it, a fusion drawn from the layered German and Czech history of Opava. Seven weights come in upright, slanted and extra-slanted cuts plus a variable version with weight and slant axes. Distinctive enough for identity work that wants historical weight without going fully gothic.
foundry_blurb: Obrysy describes Troppau as drawing its proportions from geometric sans and engaging them with sharp blackletter insets, a fusion inspired by the historical context of the Czech city Opava, which evolved through periods of German influence.

name: Plastic
classification_notes: Exaggerated, hook-shaped serifs referencing plastic toy chains from communist-era Czechoslovakia place this as a decorative display face rather than a text serif.
summary: A decorative variable display face inspired by the plastic hook-chain toys of communist-era Czechoslovakia.
description: Plastic takes its cue from 'Céčka', a fad for collecting C-shaped plastic hooks in 1980s Czechoslovakia that kids strung into bracelets and necklaces. The Chain cut plays up the hooked serif shapes for display use, while Simple strips them back for smaller sizes. Built as a variable font across weight and a 'gaps' axis controlling how open the hooks read.
foundry_blurb: Obrysy traces Plastic's inspiration to 'Céčka' fever, a phenomenon of collecting C-shaped plastic hooks in communist Czechoslovakia that became toys for 1980s children making colourful bracelets and necklaces.

name: Maskul
classification_notes: A variable font interpolating between high and low stroke contrast, named after a racehorse, places this as a display serif built around a contrast axis.
summary: A variable serif that interpolates between sensuous high contrast and firm low contrast, named after a Czech racehorse.
description: Maskul runs a contrast axis alongside weight, so the same family stretches from an elegant, high-contrast display cut down to a firm, low-contrast style usable at smaller sizes. Six weights across four contrast levels give it real range for editorial and display work. Italics are planned but not yet released.
foundry_blurb: Obrysy explains that Maskul explores interpolation between sensuous high contrast and firm low contrast extremes, named after the successful Czech racing horse 'Maskul' (1994-2017).

name: Aform
classification_notes: A decorative geometric sans drawing on post-war geometric abstraction, with unicase and ornament sets, places this firmly as a display face.
summary: A decorative geometric sans reinterpreting the visual language of post-war abstract art movements.
description: Aform reworks the form-based vocabulary of post-war geometric abstraction into a decorative display alphabet, with small capitals, unicase, ornaments and ten stylistic sets. It's a single-style face built for personality rather than a working weight range. Best suited to identity and editorial display use.
foundry_blurb: Obrysy describes Aform as a geometric sans-serif typeface inspired by the form-based aesthetics of post-war artistic movements, rooted in geometric abstraction, reinterpreting that vocabulary into a decorative display font.
